project.name: MI-13: the complete spectral-middle-factor rectangular commutator inequality
project.description: Full complex rectangular MI-13 inequality with coefficient two, actual Euclidean operator and Frobenius norms and the two largest actual singular values. All ranks, both dimension orderings and every m,n at least two are retained.

affiliations.George Stepaniants: Department of Computing and Mathematical Sciences, California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, California, USA

sources.title: MI-13 — Nobori's spectral-middle-factor commutator conjecture
sources.location: Complete original problem and repository resolution
sources.note: Exact original target formalized; original repository reduction and attribution retained. No new authorship of the informal reduction is inferred.

sources.title: A generalization of the Böttcher–Wenzel inequality for three rectangular matrices
sources.location: Conjecture 3.1, equation (8), as identified in the canonical page
sources.note: Original question and attribution retained. This draft reads the complete canonical statement and reduction; it does not claim a new audit of the external paper.

sources.title: Variance bounds, with an application to norm bounds for commutators
sources.location: Section 7.4, Corollary 5, as identified in the canonical page
sources.note: The refined commutator bound is proved internally in Lean by a finite spectral and SVD argument; the literature theorem is not assumed.

sources.title: A note on some upper bounds for the Frobenius norm of the q-deformed commutator
sources.location: Theorem 1.1 and section 3, as identified in the canonical page
sources.note: The canonical page records an alternative established route; no theorem from this paper is imported or assumed by this draft.

related_formalizations.note: Pinned actual Euclidean maps, ordered singular values, Gram eigenbases, orthonormal extension, Rayleigh extrema, complex unit-circle lemmas and block algebra are genuinely reused.
Actual kernel-mode exact half positivity and normalization certificate; positivity is consumed by the Frobenius averaging proof. All variable inequalities remain symbolic; no interval subdivision.
Challenge and numerical-boundary patterns read. No mathematical result imported.
Exact retained Challenge snapshot read and byte-bound. No fresh head query or Schiffer theorem import is claimed.

methods.tool_setup: Parallel source and independent referee agents. The coordinator alone runs local Lean serially with one thread and a 4096 MiB limit. Two exact statement reviews and independent local-run evidence audit are retained. Final Comparator, default-kernel and sandbox checks require a real non-root GitHub Linux runner.
methods.prompting_notes: Seal numerical statements and the concrete definition plan before Lean statements; obtain two independent statement approvals and actual elaboration before freezing or proof implementation. Avoid rank-counting, full commutator eigenbasis construction and interval subdivision.

automation.notes: Exact numerical and mathematical statements preceded implementation, with two independent statement approvals and actual elaboration. Source development and debugging used one serial local Lean process. Final source reviews and non-root Linux Comparator are separate recorded gates; neither a source scan nor an evidence audit is an execution.

fidelity.divergences: The exact original target is retained. The refined commutator inequality is proved internally. Sum-index padding into m+n replaces the informal max(m,n) padding, with proved preservation of actual norms and every zero-extended singular value.

review.status: Two full nonauthor proof reviews accepted on exact local53 source; independent canonical package review in progress.
review.notes: Both reports read all 22 implementation inputs and all 36 exact contracts and authenticate actual local evidence. Neither is a fresh referee compiler run or Linux Comparator execution. Apply pinned Tau Ceti guidance within these recorded scopes, with no official endorsement or human peer-review claim. See reviews/INDEX.json.
